action: The instructor introduces the lighting and presentation chapter with a title slide.
why: Orient the viewer to the final presentation stage.

action: The instructor displays a warning slide encouraging viewers to follow the lesson throughout.
why: Emphasize the importance of the lesson.

action: The instructor transitions from a photograph about lighting and storytelling to the next lighting principles slide.
why: Introduce deliberate lighting choices.

action: The instructor presents three differently lit portraits alongside the goals of mood, depth and visual focus.
why: Explain the visual purposes of lighting.

action: The instructor points at the lit portrait and its eyes while comparing the examples.
why: Show how light reveals volume and draws attention toward the face.

action: The instructor points to the face in another portrait reference.
why: Illustrate the face as a visual focal point.

action: The instructor switches from the portrait examples to a backlit composition photograph.
view: portrait references then backlit side view
why: Connect lighting decisions with composition.

action: The instructor displays a backlit subject while discussing how framing, camera angle and focal length affect the lighting.
why: Evaluate lighting in the context of the chosen camera.
reader_equivalent: Set and aim a camera with exec_python, then inspect with render_image.

action: The instructor displays a grid of cinematic images as lighting and composition references.
why: Use existing images as guides rather than guessing.

action: The instructor shows an outdoor environment image and four material spheres to explain image-based lighting.
why: Illustrate environment illumination and its dependence on the source image.
reader_equivalent: Use exec_python to connect an Environment Texture to the world background.

action: The instructor points to the sun in the environment image.
why: Show that the light source is baked into the image rather than independently movable.
reader_equivalent: Use exec_python to load and rotate an environment texture.

action: The instructor adds a point light among sample objects and switches to rendered viewport shading.
why: Demonstrate a local light on surrounding objects.
reader_equivalent: Create a POINT light with exec_python and inspect using viewport_capture with rendered shading.

action: The instructor opens the selected point light's data properties and increases its power while watching the rendered viewport.
why: Show how the power control changes illumination.
reader_equivalent: Set the point light data energy with exec_python and inspect the render.

action: The instructor moves the point light among the sample objects and changes perspective to inspect the radiating shadows.
view: rendered user perspective including overhead view
why: Show that point light spreads in every direction and objects block it.
reader_equivalent: Move a POINT light with exec_python and inspect the result with viewport_capture.

action: The instructor examines the point-lit objects from another angle before returning to a light-types slide.
view: rendered user perspective then point-light illustration
why: Summarize the point light demonstration.
reader_equivalent: Inspect a POINT light with viewport_capture.

action: The instructor adjusts a spotlight's radius while watching the shadows on the sample objects.
view: rendered user perspective and side view
why: Demonstrate how larger emitter radius softens shadows.
reader_equivalent: Change a SPOT light's shadow_soft_size with exec_python and compare renders.

action: The instructor adds an area light over the sample objects and raises its power in the rendered viewport.
tool: Area light and Light Data Properties
why: Demonstrate a controllable softbox-like character light.
reader_equivalent: Create an AREA light and set its size and energy with exec_python.

action: The instructor changes from spotlight and area-light illustrations to the three-point-lighting introduction.
why: Transition from individual light types to a lighting arrangement.

action: The instructor shows two stylized-character images while introducing three-point lighting as a starting arrangement.
why: Encourage learning a baseline before exploring different lighting designs.
reader_equivalent: Create a key, fill and rim with exec_python, then iterate from the camera view.

action: The instructor points at a stylized character example while discussing variation beyond a standard lighting setup.
why: Relate lighting style to storytelling.

action: The instructor switches to a grayscale bust illustrating illumination from a key light.
why: Show how the main light creates prominent highlights and shadows.
reader_equivalent: Create and aim an AREA key light using exec_python.

action: The instructor points to shadowed areas of the key-lit bust and introduces the fill light.
why: Contrast the form-defining key with a shadow-lifting fill.
reader_equivalent: Compare key-only and fill-only renders with render_image.

action: The instructor compares a dim bust image against the brighter key-lit version while describing fill on the opposite side.
why: Illustrate controlling the depth of key-light shadows.
reader_equivalent: Place a weaker AREA fill opposite the key using exec_python and compare renders.

action: The instructor displays the grayscale bust with a blue rim outlining the hat and shoulder.
view: grayscale bust with blue edge light
why: Show separation from the background and controlled contrast.
reader_equivalent: Aim a colored rim light from behind using exec_python and inspect a render.

action: The instructor introduces post-processing with a compositor example that changes a chromatic-aberration effect on an image.
why: Show that finishing occurs after lighting and rendering.
reader_equivalent: Use exec_python to create compositor nodes and inspect the output.

action: The slide's compositor example cycles through chromatic-aberration controls on a rendered image.
why: Illustrate optical finishing effects that can make a render feel less synthetic.
reader_equivalent: Use a compositor Lens Distortion node through exec_python as a comparable fringing effect.

action: The slide continues showing a chromatic-aberration node being adjusted on a rendered image.
why: Reinforce the contribution of finishing to the final image.
reader_equivalent: Use exec_python to configure compositor finishing nodes and compare the result.

action: The instructor orbits around the posed character and shows two pose assets in Blender's Asset Browser.
view: user perspective from side and front
why: Review the available presentation poses before lighting.
reader_equivalent: Set a known posed frame and inspect with viewport_capture.

action: The instructor hides visible rig controls and zooms out to inspect the posed character unobstructed.
why: Clear the viewport for lighting and presentation work.
reader_equivalent: Hide rig controls in the viewport with exec_python while preserving character deformation.

action: The instructor closes the asset pane and opens the Add menu at Camera beside an existing camera.
view: user perspective showing full character and camera object
why: Begin setting a camera angle before placing lights.
reader_equivalent: Create and aim a camera with exec_python, or use the existing scene camera.

action: Camera is locked to the viewport (lock icon at the viewport's right edge) so orbiting moves the camera; character stands small inside the grey camera frame.
why: Steer the camera by navigating the view instead of typing transforms.
reader_equivalent: add_camera(...) then aim(); no view-lock equivalent

action: Opens Output properties then selects the camera: output shows 1200 x 1500 at 100%, 24 fps, PNG RGBA 8-bit; then Camera data tab with default 50 mm lens.
view: User perspective then camera perspective (portrait frame)
why: Show that resolution decides the frame shape and that the lens is changed per camera.
reader_equivalent: sc.render.resolution_x, resolution_y = 1200, 1500; cam.data.lens = 138

action: Drags the Focal Length field wider and wider; frame zooms to the torso at about 143 mm, settles at 138 mm; tooltip for Focal Length shown.
why: Long lens to flatten the face and fit the character into the portrait frame.
reader_equivalent: cd = cam.data; cd.lens = 138.0

action: Switches the camera view from rendered to solid, repositions the camera so the full body sits slightly below centre; hair looks like dots while rendering; later pulls back to a user view showing the camera's frame floating at foot level.
tool: Viewport navigation, shading toggle, camera move (G)
view: Camera perspective, rendered then solid; user perspective
why: Place the figure in frame by eye before any lighting.
reader_equivalent: add_camera('camera_wideshot', box, 0, 1, azimuth_deg=15)

action: Turns the viewport gizmos off, unlocks camera-to-view, and splits into two views: left user perspective, right camera view; the right one goes to rendered shading and starts showing a grey empty frame.
tool: Viewport layout / Lock Camera to View off / shading popover
view: Left: user perspective solid; right: camera view rendered
why: Unlock so the camera isn't moved by accident; keep a second live camera view for lighting.
reader_equivalent: viewport_capture(camera='camera_wideshot', shading='RENDERED')

action: In the rendered view's shading popover, both Scene Lights and Scene World are ticked; then opens World properties: Surface Background with a dark grey Color and Strength 1.000; render shows the figure very dark.
view: Right pane: camera view, rendered shading
why: Make the preview use the scene's own light and world rather than the viewport studio light.
reader_equivalent: bpy.context.scene.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs['Strength'].default_value = 1.0

action: Adds a plane, scales it up in Edit Mode, extrudes the back edge up with E then Z, bevels the corner with Ctrl B (header: Offset 1.08 m, Segments 6, Profile Shape 0.5), then right-clicks Shade Smooth; backdrop is light grey.
tool: Plane, Extrude (E Z), Bevel (Ctrl B), Shade Smooth
view: User perspective, solid; right pane rendered
why: First attempt at a studio sweep with no seam at the corner.
reader_equivalent: make_backdrop(box) builds the sweep in bmesh; bevel arguments inferred

action: Shade smooth is applied; then viewed from a low side angle: the plane's edge shows, so the artist drops the plane approach.
view: User perspective, solid, with the camera panel visible
why: Show that a plane backdrop exposes its edge to a side camera.

action: Deletes the plane (Delete confirmation), opens Add > Mesh > Circle and adds a circle outline around the character.
why: Replace the plane with a circle so it can wrap around the character.
reader_equivalent: bmesh circle fan in make_backdrop

action: In Edit Mode fills the circle, scales it up (S, scale about 1.18 to 1.23 in the header), selects the rim verts in top orthographic with a box, then extrudes the whole rim up (Dz about 0.96 m) into a cylindrical wall.
tool: Edit Mode: Fill (F), Scale (S), Box Select, Extrude (E Z)
why: Build floor and wall in one mesh.
reader_equivalent: make_backdrop(radius_f=1.6, wall_f=2.5)

action: Bevels the floor/wall corner edge ring with Ctrl B (header: Offset 0.345 m then 0.382 m, Segments 6, Profile Shape 0.5), scrolling to add segments; the corner becomes a curved sweep and the floor turns pale from the render lighting.
view: User perspective, solid, close to the floor
why: Round the floor-to-wall corner so no horizon line is visible.
reader_equivalent: bmesh sweep rows in make_backdrop (sweep=8, rb=0.35*H)

action: Smooth-shaded closed cylinder backdrop viewed from outside; hovers over the outliner, presses C to start a new collection, and opens the Screencast Keys add-on panel to show the keys.
tool: Outliner: New Collection (C); Screencast Keys add-on
why: Keep render objects apart from the character collection.
reader_equivalent: collection('RENDER')

action: New collection renamed RENDER; drags the Circle mesh and then the Camera into it (tooltip: Move inside collection, Ctrl to link, Shift to parent). Camera frustum goes orange when selected.
tool: Outliner drag and drop, F2/double-click rename
why: Group the backdrop, camera and lights in one collection.
reader_equivalent: collection('RENDER').objects.link(ob)

action: Renames Circle to backdrop; orbits (Alt+mouse) around the cylinder showing wall and bevelled floor sweep; flat floor and the camera sit inside.
why: Name the objects so later steps can find them.
reader_equivalent: ob.name = 'backdrop'

action: Selects the backdrop, notes the Material tab is empty (New button); orbits, then presses Shift+A to open the Add menu (Mesh submenu open).
view: User perspective; Properties on Material tab
why: Material is deferred until lighting exists.

action: Shift+A > Light > Area; Area properties show Power 10.000 W, Exposure 0.000, Normalize ticked, Shape Square, Size 1 m, Spread 180 deg; renames it light_key, then presses C in the outliner and names a child collection lights.
view: User perspective, solid; outliner and Light properties
why: Start the key light and keep lights tidy in a child collection.
reader_equivalent: add_light('light_key','AREA',...) inside collection('lights', collection('RENDER'))

action: Moves the key light up beside the character (G, R rotation header 41.11) while holding Ctrl+Alt; render pane flips from black to noisy lit; then orbits into the head and the render shows the face lit from the side.
view: Left: user perspective then close orbit; right: rendered
why: Aim the key at the face from the side and above.
reader_equivalent: add_light('light_key','AREA', polar(box,40*s,0.75*H,1.15), head_target)

action: Selects the hair curve, opens Modifiers: GeometryNodes with Viewport Amount reduced to 0.05 (field typed at 19:30:34).
tool: Modifiers panel > Viewport Amount on the hair GeometryNodes modifier
view: Left: close orbit on the hair; right: rendered
why: Keep viewport responsive while lighting.
reader_equivalent: hair_modifier['Viewport Amount'] = 0.05 (input key name per hair stage)

action: Back on light_key: drags Power from 10 up; fields read about 17.9 W as the render brightens; tooltip describes Power in watts.
why: Brighten the key without overexposing.
reader_equivalent: light.data.energy = value

action: Power reads 17.900 then 16.700 as the artist backs off; orbits the left view to a frontal angle; render looks lit but not blown out.
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered camera view
why: Judge exposure from the render pane, stop before overexposure.
reader_equivalent: light.data.energy = 16.7

action: Switches to Top orthographic (Numpad 7) and moves/rotates (G then R) the key light; right pane is a closer crop, sample count low so noise is heavy; light then reads about 16.7 W.
view: Left: top orthographic; right: rendered close crop
why: Place the light's side and angle from above, check on the face.
reader_equivalent: aim(light, head); polar(box, 40*side, ...)

action: Key power now reads 18.200; Shift+A > Light > Area creates a second light (Area.001, Power 10 W), moved to the other side (G) and rotated twice (R R trackball); render goes noisy and bright.
tool: Add > Light > Area, Move (G), Rotate (R x2)
why: Create the fill light opposite the key.
reader_equivalent: add_light('light_fill','AREA', polar(box,-55*s,1.0*H,0.85), chest, 1.4*k, size=1.3*H)

action: Zooms the render pane on the face: with the fill at 10 W the image looks flat; drags the fill Power down to about 1.9 W.
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered face close-up
why: Show that equal power kills the shadows.
reader_equivalent: fill.data.energy = 1.4

action: Compares fill hidden vs visible by toggling its render eye in the outliner; fill power moves 1.900 to 1.400; shadows lighten but remain.
why: A/B check: the fill must lift but not remove shadows.
reader_equivalent: fill.hide_render toggle; energy 1.4

action: Fill power reads 1.160 after one more drag; double-clicks the light in the outliner and renames it light_fill (data still named Area.001); the left view orbits to a wider cylinder view.
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered close-up
why: Name the light for later reference.
reader_equivalent: ob.name = 'light_fill'; ld.energy = 1.16

action: Scales the fill (S, header 1.3712) then hides it; selects light_key and scales it down with S (header 0.1862): shadows on the face get sharper, key power reads 18.200.
tool: Scale (S) on area lights; outliner hide
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered face
why: Demonstrate that light size controls shadow softness.
reader_equivalent: light.data.size = <value>

action: Toggles Size slider and scale on light_key (power 18.200, Size 1 m) with Clear Scale in the redo bar; render noise changes with each edit; then shows light_fill again via the outliner eye.
tool: Light data > Size; Object Scale; outliner eye
view: Left: side view of head; right: rendered face
why: Same effect through object scale or the Size field.
reader_equivalent: ld.size changes

action: Selects light_fill, scales it up (S, header 1.4421, Shift for precision) so shadows vanish, and raises Power to 1.360; render pane then zooms out to a full body.
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered close then full body
why: Make the fill big so it casts no shadow of its own.
reader_equivalent: light_fill scale / size; energy 1.36

action: Orbits the render pane from the full body to a face crop; Ctrl, Ctrl+Alt, Shift+Alt held (viewport navigation); fill still 1.360; the artist notes lower legs need more light.
view: Left: user perspective; right: rendered, close and wide
why: Check key and fill together on face and body.
reader_equivalent: render_image after build

action: Fill selected, then Shift+A adds a third Area light (Area.002, 10 W); switches to Right orthographic (Numpad 3), rotates it (R, 91.45) and moves it (G) to sit behind and low; render shows white hair rim light starting.
tool: Add > Light > Area, Numpad 3, Rotate (R), Move (G)
why: Create the rim light behind the character.
reader_equivalent: add_light('light_rim','AREA', polar(box,-145*s,0.9*H,0.7), chest, 50*k, rim_colour, size=0.3*H, size_y=1.3*H)

action: The artist raises the selected area rim light's power while monitoring the rendered character.
view: solid scene view alongside rendered camera view
why: Strengthen the edge separation from the backdrop.
reader_equivalent: Set the rim light's data.energy through exec_python and inspect with viewport_capture.

action: The artist narrows the rim area light along its local X axis while checking the edge in the camera preview.
view: overhead scene view and rendered camera view
why: Concentrate the rim toward one side instead of spreading it broadly.
reader_equivalent: Adjust the rim object's local X scale using exec_python and inspect the rendered camera.

action: The artist rotates the narrow rim light around global Z while watching the rendered figure.
view: high oblique scene view and rendered camera view
why: Aim the light to graze the character's side.
reader_equivalent: Adjust rim rotation with exec_python and compare rendered camera previews.

action: The artist checks the rim-lit full-body camera image and points out a bright patch on the floor backdrop.
view: top then oblique scene view beside full-body rendered camera view
why: Identify unwanted rim spill on the backdrop.
reader_equivalent: Inspect viewport_capture(camera="camera_wideshot", shading="RENDERED") for backdrop spill.

action: With the rim light active, the artist drags the backdrop from the Outliner into the light-linking receiver list.
tool: Object Properties Light Linking and Outliner
view: oblique solid scene and rendered full-body camera view
why: Make the backdrop a receiver that can be excluded from the rim.
reader_equivalent: Assign a receiver collection containing the backdrop to the rim using exec_python.

action: The artist switches the backdrop receiver from include to exclude in the rim light's linking list.
view: solid scene and rendered full-body camera view
why: Remove the rim's bright floor spill while retaining its effect on the character.
reader_equivalent: Set the backdrop collection object's light_linking.link_state to EXCLUDE in exec_python.

action: The artist chooses a dark warm backdrop material and raises its roughness while watching the camera preview.
view: oblique solid studio view and rendered full-body camera view
why: Give the background a subdued, less reflective finish.
reader_equivalent: Adjust backdrop Principled BSDF Base Color and Roughness with exec_python.

action: The artist lowers backdrop specular response and begins setting a camera-view render border.
tool: Material Properties and 3D Viewport render region
view: rendered full-body camera beside solid scene view
why: Reduce background highlights and focus the preview on the composition.
reader_equivalent: Adjust the backdrop shader's Specular IOR Level using exec_python and inspect the camera render.

action: The artist limits the rendered preview to the camera frame and opens the camera's viewport-display settings.
tool: 3D Viewport render region and Camera Properties
view: full-body rendered camera and oblique solid scene
why: Remove distracting content outside the composition.
reader_equivalent: Set camera.data.passepartout_alpha with exec_python and inspect the camera view.

action: The artist raises camera passepartout to full opacity and adjusts the full-body composition.
view: portrait rendered camera view with black surround
why: Judge the shot without the scene outside the frame.
reader_equivalent: Set camera.data.passepartout_alpha = 1.0 and adjust its transform with exec_python.

action: The artist orbits around the studio and selects the key light after reviewing the basic full-body setup.
view: oblique solid scene view alongside rendered camera
why: Prepare to add lower-body illumination using another light.
reader_equivalent: Select or access the key object with exec_python and inspect its contribution with viewport_capture.

action: The artist positions a duplicated key light lower down, checking it from above and in the rendered camera.
view: top orthographic then oblique solid scene alongside rendered full-body camera
why: Lift the comparatively dark legs.
reader_equivalent: Duplicate the area light and adjust its transform with exec_python, then inspect the camera render.

action: The artist lowers the power of two key lights that share a light datablock while evaluating the portrait.
view: solid scene and rendered full-body camera
why: Balance the combined illumination from the two key positions.
reader_equivalent: Assign the same light datablock to both objects and set its energy with exec_python.

action: The artist experiments with the rim light's color picker, moving from white through warm and cool colors.
view: solid scene and rendered full-body camera
why: Compare colored edge lighting against the character and backdrop.
reader_equivalent: Change rim.data.color through exec_python and compare rendered views.

action: The artist settles on a warm orange-red rim and starts repositioning a fill light.
tool: Light Properties color picker and 3D Viewport
view: oblique solid scene and rendered full-body camera
why: Add a warm edge and refine the balance of the fill.
reader_equivalent: Set rim.data.color to the corresponding linear RGB and adjust the fill transform using exec_python.

action: The artist hides a fill light, selects the key, and zooms in on the face while moving the light.
view: top orthographic scene and enlarged rendered camera face
why: Isolate the key and inspect unwanted facial shadows.
reader_equivalent: Temporarily hide the fill and adjust the key transform with exec_python; capture the face in rendered view.

action: From top and front views the artist moves and rotates the key while inspecting a close-up of the face.
view: top and front scene views beside rendered face close-up
why: Bring some key light onto the far side rather than splitting the face into two halves.
reader_equivalent: Reposition and aim the key with exec_python and inspect a close-up rendered capture.

action: The artist restores the previously hidden light and zooms back out from the face to assess the full composition.
view: rendered face close-up transitioning to full-body camera
why: Check the corrected key in combination with the other lights.
reader_equivalent: Restore the fill's visibility and inspect close-up and wide rendered captures.

action: The artist opens Add Light and selects the point-light option for an additional backdrop light.
view: oblique solid studio and rendered full-body camera
why: Add a separate controllable source for the backdrop.
reader_equivalent: Create a POINT light with bpy.data.lights.new through exec_python.

action: The artist duplicates and rotates a fill light near the floor after inspecting the orange backdrop glow and shadows.
view: oblique and overhead solid studio beside rendered full-body camera
why: Reduce distracting cast shadows on the backdrop.
reader_equivalent: Duplicate and aim a fill area light at the shadowed backdrop using exec_python.

action: The artist reviews the completed lighting and selects the hair's geometry-nodes viewport amount for a fuller preview.
view: solid studio and rendered full-body camera
why: Judge the lighting with the hair displayed more fully.
reader_equivalent: Adjust the groom modifier's viewport density input with exec_python and capture the rendered camera.

action: The artist darkens the backdrop base color, then opens World Properties.
tool: Material Properties color picker and World Properties
view: solid studio and rendered portrait camera
why: Refine the backdrop before adding ambient illumination.
reader_equivalent: Adjust backdrop Principled BSDF Base Color through exec_python.

action: The artist examines the existing dark world background color before choosing an environmental light.
view: rendered full-body camera and solid scene overview
why: Plan a dim ambient source to lift areas that are otherwise too dark.
reader_equivalent: Inspect the world Background node through exec_python; set_world can configure ambient lighting.

action: The artist shows the Poly Haven nature HDRI browser and switches back to the original World datablock.
view: asset browser below studio view beside rendered portrait camera
why: Contrast the add-on environment with the ordinary world setup.
reader_equivalent: Use exec_python to connect a downloaded environment image to the world Background node.

action: The artist revisits the dark backdrop color while assessing the full-body lighting in the camera.
view: solid studio overview and rendered portrait camera
why: Fine-tune the background against the finished lighting.
reader_equivalent: Adjust the backdrop material with exec_python and compare rendered captures.

action: The artist reviews the three-point demonstration in the rendered portrait camera.
view: solid studio overview and rendered full-body portrait
why: Present the current setup as a starting point before a different final cinematic look.
reader_equivalent: Use viewport_capture(camera="camera_wideshot", shading="RENDERED") to judge the setup.

action: The artist closes the asset-browser area and navigates closer to the character and lighting rig.
view: solid studio overview zooming toward character and rendered wide camera
why: Prepare to create additional camera angles.
reader_equivalent: Use scene inspection and viewport_capture before placing another camera.

action: The artist reduces the hair viewport amount, renames the wide camera, and duplicates it for another shot.
tool: Geometry Nodes modifier and Outliner duplicate
view: close solid character view and rendered full-body camera
why: Keep navigation responsive while preparing a second composition.
reader_equivalent: Set the groom modifier's viewport amount and duplicate the camera with exec_python.

action: The artist adjusts the duplicated camera to frame a closer head-and-torso portrait.
tool: Camera Properties and camera view navigation
view: solid close-up scene and rendered portrait camera
why: Provide a closer shot in addition to the full-body view.
reader_equivalent: Create and position camera_closeup with a 138 mm lens through exec_python and inspect its render.

action: The artist duplicates the close-up camera and reframes toward the skirt and legs to demonstrate an optional detail shot.
view: solid character scene beside rendered portrait detail camera
why: Show how additional compositions can feature modeled costume details.
reader_equivalent: Duplicate the close-up camera and adjust its transform for a detail view with exec_python.
